title: Saying it instead of typing it
description: POST /v1/voice. The browser records, this machine transcribes, and the words land in the composer's box and stop there. Nothing on this path can reach a terminal, which is what makes a dictation that heard the wrong thing a typo rather than an incident.

VoiceRequest.description: A recording, already in the one shape whisper.cpp takes. The resampling is done in the browser because that is the one format question every browser can answer about itself — what it just recorded — while this machine has no ffmpeg and could not open an Opus file if it wanted to.

audio.description: Base64 of little-endian 16-bit mono PCM. A minute of it is about 2.6MB encoded.

rate.description: Must be 16000. Checked rather than resampled: a body that names 48000 has not made a small mistake, it has sent something that would transcribe as a voice three times too fast, and quietly resampling somebody's voice is a worse answer than saying no.

VoiceResult.description: What was said, and how long this machine took to read it. An empty `text` is an answer and not a failure: whisper heard the recording and there were no words in it, which happens to a pocket and to a room that went quiet.

text.description: The transcript to use: the cleaned text when `polish.status` is `applied`, otherwise Whisper's own.

raw.description: Whisper's own text, present only when a cleanup replaced it, so the composer can offer it back.

VoicePolish.description: What happened to the optional cleanup turn after Whisper. Absent when cleanup is off. Every status other than `applied` means `text` is Whisper's own.

status.description: `applied`, `unchanged`, `unavailable` (the chosen assistant is not installed), `unfaithful` (the cleanup changed the words and was discarded), `too_long`, `quota`, `timeout` or `failed`.

assistant.description: `claude` or `codex`: whose account the turn used.

ms.description: How long the cleanup turn took.

VoiceLanguage.description: GET /v1/voice/language: what the next recording will be read as, and who said so. `auto` follows Clawdline's own language (the `language` setting), then this machine's languages, then the catalog this daemon ships; the settings window says the answer back, so a Simplified transcript is never a surprise nobody could have seen coming.

setting.description: `voice_language` as the settings file has it: `auto`, or a tag.

code.description: What whisper is given as `-l`: `zh`, another two-letter code, or `auto` for whisper's own detection.

script.description: How Chinese in the answer is written: `Hant`, `Hans`, or empty when nothing said, which is whisper's own habit and Simplified.

source.description: Who decided `code`: `voice_language`, `language`, `AppleLanguages`, `AppleLocale`, `LANGUAGE`, `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES`, `LANG`, `Windows`, `catalog`, or empty when nobody did.

tag.description: The tag that source gave, as it spelled it.

script_source.description: Who decided `script`, in the same words as `source`; empty when nobody did.

VoiceSource.description: GET /v1/voice/source: the machine whose Whisper will read the next recording. The composer uses this only as a quiet source label; a failure to read it never prevents dictation.

machine.description: The authenticated Cloud machine id, or empty on a page served directly by this machine.

name.description: The machine's display name, bounded by the UI before it is shown.

VoiceSetup.description: GET /v1/voice/setup: what this machine has for local dictation, where it looked, and the exact supported way to add the missing pieces. Paths under the current home directory are written with ~ so this response carries no account path.

binary.description: The executable file name in use, or empty.

model.description: The model file name in use, or empty.

binary_dirs.description: Directories searched for whisper-cli, with the home directory written as ~.

model_dirs.description: Directories searched for ggml models, with the home directory written as ~.

binary_install.description: A command, or commands separated by newlines, that install the compatible whisper.cpp CLI on this platform. The Python openai-whisper command is intentionally never offered.

model_name.description: The pinned model the POST action downloads.

polish_assistants.description: Which assistants could clean up a transcript on this machine: `claude`, `codex`, both or neither.

vocabulary_builtin.description: The names every transcript is repaired against without being asked.

vocabulary_projects.description: The project folder names `voice_vocabulary_projects` would add, listed so the person sees exactly what a ticked box sends.

VoiceModelInstall.description: POST /v1/voice/setup after the pinned model has been downloaded, size-checked, SHA-256 checked and atomically installed.

model.description: The installed model file name; its private path is not returned.

VoiceRefusal.description: A refusal from this route. It is the ordinary refusal shape with one field added, because `no_whisper` covers two different afternoons: `brew install whisper-cpp` leaves a machine with the binary and no model, and a page told only "no whisper" sends somebody to check the thing they already did.
